results.question: When a well stays shut in longer than the repair itself, what are we usually waiting on: parts, crews, contractors or weather? Break it down by area for jobs started in 2026, with the typical number of extra days, and tell me if any area stands out.

response.summary: 474 jobs have an explicit report statement quantifying extra shut-in waiting. Southeast Block 31 has the highest area median (10 extra days). This is a descriptive comparison, not proof of an area's operational quality; equipment mix and reporting coverage can differ.

results.question: Which region of the field consistently runs hotter?

response.summary: Assuming “hotter” means operational wellhead temperatures, I compared 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, using producing readings, each well equally weighted within type/month. Raw wellhead means are highest in Southeast; raw heat mixes weather, lift type and operation. After subtracting ambient and equally weighting the 36 type/month strata present in every region, Southwest has the highest mean delta, but is hottest in 17/36 comparisons. There is no region that is universally hottest across all matched type/month comparisons. This does not establish reservoir heat or oil output.
response.methodology: Compare within historical well type and month, use well-month means, ambient-adjust, and equal-weight common strata. Nonproducing readings excluded.
